notes: Auth: the firebase CLI login (a project owner), so beginTransaction gives a PESSIMISTIC read-write transaction and security rules do not apply.
T1 is always begun before T2 (T1 is the older transaction). A read is GET with ?transaction=; a write is commit with one update of fields {writer, step}.

Each event has startMs and endMs from the start of its run, latencyMs, and timing "waited" when latencyMs >= 3000, otherwise "fast". Times differ on every recording; outcomes, statuses, messages and patterns are what must match.

A request still pending after 5000 ms (25000 ms in s6) is treated as blocked and the scenario goes on; client-side timeouts are 15000 ms, or 40000 ms for a request expected to block. A client timeout is recorded as outcome clientTimeout.
transactions: per actor, committed / aborted (with the operation and message) / rolled back. final: each document's writer after the run (GET without transaction).

pattern: a run's requests (without begins) and results; timingPattern adds fast/waited. summary[scenario].stable is true when the runs have the same pattern, timingStable when they have the same timingPattern (network jitter alone can push an ordinary read past the threshold).
Transaction ids are replaced by <T1 transaction id> and so on; times by placeholders (normalise in lib.mjs); messages are as returned.
s5 and s5probe ran in parallel with the other scenarios, on their own documents; the probes (50 s and 65 s idle) bound the idle limit.
